steps.title: Prepare Paraffin Embedded Cell Line Pellets
steps.instruction: Process the cell suspension into a solid pellet for paraffin embedding.

substeps.instruction: Spin the cell suspension at 1800 rpm for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Add 5 ml of 70% ethanol for 30 minutes and vortex mildly.
Repeat the decanting and ethanol treatment using 100% ethanol until a very solid pellet is obtained.
Carefully pull the cell pellet out of the tube using a clean wooden applicator stick and place it into a cassette lined with black biopsy filter paper.

steps.title: Perform N-Cadherin Immunohistochemical Staining
steps.instruction: Conduct immunohistochemical staining for N-Cadherin following the manufacturer's instructions.

steps.title: Conduct Wound Healing Assay
steps.instruction: Assess the migration of SCC cell lines following treatment with safranal.

substeps.instruction: Plate SCC cell line in 24-well plates and grow to confluence.
Remove media and create a scratch using a 100 μl pipette tip.
Wash with PBS and treat with sub-toxic concentrations of safranal for 24 h.
Observe and photograph wounds at 0 h (before treatment) and 48 h (after treatment) using a stereo microscope fitted with a digital camera.
Calculate wound healing as the percentage of the initial wound until total wound closure at the 48 h time point.
Repeat the assay three independent times.

steps.title: Perform MTT Assay for Viability and Cytotoxicity
steps.instruction: Measure cell viability and cytotoxicity using the MTT assay.

substeps.instruction: Plate 1 ml of cells (50,000 - 100,000 cells/ml) into each well of a 96-well culture plate for 24 hours.
Incubate cells for 24 h in a CO2 incubator.
Treat cells with antibiotics and antifungal for 24-72 h, then remove experimental media and wash with PBS.
Add safranal to cell lines, incubate for 48 hours, and wash twice with PBS.
Incubate cells with medium containing 0.5 mg/ml MTT in a CO2 incubator at 37°C for 4 h.
Aspirate the medium and solubilize the formazan product with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Measure absorbance at 570 nm for each well using a microplate reader (BioTek, Flx 800).
Calculate % cytotoxicity as 1 - [mean absorbance of treated cells / mean absorbance of negative control] and % viability as 100 - % cytotoxicity.

description: 2 II. Introduction: 6a. Statement of the problem: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the head and neck is the sixth most common cancer in humans worldwide, nearly more than half a million new cases per year occur. Although treatment improved over the last decades, the five -year survival rate is approximately 50%, which remains one of the lowest among other common cancer types (Jonsson et al., 2012; Jabini et al., 2017). Despite the important function of chemotherapy in the treatment of cancer, severe side effects are encountered maki ng its clinical application limited. So, it is necessary to search for new anticancer substances with high ef ficacy and minimal side effects (Jabini et al., 2017). Chemopreventive agents made from natural products may be used as alternative and safe cancer treatment options in comparison to the currently used anti -cancer therapies which are responsible for a wide variety of side effects besides the provided benefits (Surh, 2003; Fryer et al., 2009). Scientific Rationale The current study will investigate the effect of Safranal on the biological activities of SCC cell line; namely the epithelial -mesenchymal transition of squamous cell carcinoma cells. This will add to our knowledge about the effect of safranal on SCC, therefore providing a more effective and less toxic possible treatment for this malignancy. PICO P: Cultured human SCC cell line. I: Application of Safranal on SCC cell line. C: Cultured SCC cell line without application of Safranal. O: Assessment of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) , migration and cell viability of SCC cell line.
